The facts: Li Moujia, a tax officer, used his position to obtain blank tax payment certificates, forged 38 tax payment certificates, allowing cars to be registered without paying tax, causing tax loss. Also, he under-assessed tax for 28 vehicles, causing loss. So crimes: forging state documents (变造国家机关证件罪) and tax evasion? Actually the act of not collecting tax is "偷税漏税" which is a crime under tax law, but in criminal law, the relevant offense is "逃税罪" (tax evasion) or "偷税罪". However, the description says "对3辆不征、28辆少征购置税的行为，认为又构成××". Likely "偷税罪" (tax evasion) or "逃税罪". In Chinese criminal law, article 201 of Criminal Law: "偷税漏税罪" (tax evasion). So the crimes: 变造国家机关证件罪; 偷税漏税罪. Also possibly "徇私舞弊" is a separate offense under "徇私舞弊罪" (abuse of power for personal gain). But the typical charge for a tax official who under-collects tax is "徇私舞弊罪" (abuse of power). Actually article 395 of Criminal Law: "徇私舞弊罪" for state functionaries who, in performance of duties, accept bribes or act for personal gain, causing state losses. But here he didn't accept bribes, he just used his position to help others. The crime could be "徇私舞弊罪" (abuse of power). However the description says "对3辆不征、28辆少征购置税的行为，认为又构成××". Likely "偷税漏税罪". So answer: 变造国家机关证件罪;偷税漏税罪.
